features.note: Walled enclosure reads clearly as a boundary inside the bay. Closed state (compressor-room.png) is a solid opaque box occupying the correct corner of the bay. Open state (compressor-room-open.png) reveals all four equipment pieces inside the enclosure walls — the room IS a boundary, not open slab. Exhaust-wall shots (coupling-exhaust-off, coupling-exhaust-full) show the louver pair on the exterior face with clear blade states: shut is a dense solid-striped rectangle; open shows rotated blades (horizontal bars) with two fan-circle apertures visible behind. Fan count = 2 confirmed. Louver pair reads as a single 2.4 m-span panel divided centrally into two 1.2 m sections — consistent with exhaust_louver_count: 2 and exhaust_louver_pair_span_m: 2.4. Enclosure top is visibly below the 8 m bay clear height, reading as a 4 m inner room.

Grid structure reads as regular from the dedicated luminaire-grid view: pendant rods at even spacing, luminaires as disc/cylinder forms with white lit lenses, mounted clearly below the roof-truss lattice (trusses form the background grid, pendants hang through it). The spec promises 18 in a 6x3 grid at 7.0 m. No single capture permits a definitive count of 18 due to perspective foreshortening, but the distribution seen in the hero shot (index.png) across the full 40x20 m floor plan and the uniform column spacing in the luminaire-grid view are consistent with a 6x3 arrangement. Luminaires read as discs with bright white lenses (not emissive boxes) in all lit-state captures. Pendant attachment below trusses confirmed in both luminaire-grid.png and duct-run.png.

AHU box sits on rooftop at the correct quadrant (ahu-roof.png and index.png confirm). Supply riser connects AHU underside to trunk duct with no visible gap or floating segment in either the ahu-roof or duct-run captures — the riser-to-trunk transition at [-12, 6.8, 0] is continuous. Trunk duct (large-diameter cylinder, consistent with 0.95 m) runs the bay at high level clearly visible in all interior views. Air path reads continuous from unit to space. DEFECT: 8 diffusers along the duct (spec: diffuser_array from x=-10 to x=14 at y=6.55) are not distinguishable as individual outlet shapes in any of the 11 captures. Only the green flow-direction arrows are visible along the duct. Diffuser geometry may be present but is unresolvable at capture scale, or may be absent.

The open-room view (compressor-room-open.png) confirms all four skid elements are present in the scene: lead compressor package (left, larger dark box with circular fan-grille on face), lag compressor (adjacent dark box, similar but slightly smaller, with its own grille circle), blue cylindrical receiver, and smaller dryer box — plus a thin inter-equipment pipe. This geometry keeps the spec's promise. However, the dedicated compressor-skid preset (compressor-skid.png) fails on two counts that this lens must flag. First, the frame captures only the two compressor cabinets; the receiver and dryer are outside the right edge of the frame. The spec promise 'alongside a vertical receiver and a dryer, joined by real piping' cannot be read from the dedicated evidence shot. Second, the compressor-skid view is severely underlit: the camera angle faces surfaces that the house-rig key light cannot reach, producing a near-black image in which the cooling-fan grille circles are barely distinguishable. The promise of a legible rotary-screw identity is not kept in the one frame that must carry it.

Bay reads as a real industrial building. Column lines are visible along all four walls in the hero and interior views. Roof trusses are exposed in the open-plan default (roof layer off) and form a clear lattice at 8.0 m. Clad wall panels present on all sides with visible column-bay rhythm. Bay-envelope.png (roof on) shows the closed form: the 2:1 plan ratio (40x20 m) is visible from the isometric angle, the wall-height to wall-length ratio (~1:5 for an 8 m wall on a 40 m face) reads correctly, and the AHU box at 3.5x1.6x2.0 m occupies approximately 8.75 pct of the 40 m roofline — proportionally correct. Column-bay spacing appears consistent with the declared 8.0 m: approximately 5 bays along the long face are visible.

important_features.note: Air header piping connecting the lead compressor discharge to the receiver is visible as a thin bright pipe in compressor-room-open.png. However, the distribution main specified to run from [15.5, 2.36, -7.5] to [-14.0, 5.5, -7.5] — a 29.5 m run at varying height across the full bay — is not distinguishable in any interior or hero view. The 0.08 m header diameter is geometrically dwarfed by the 0.95 m HVAC trunk duct that dominates all interior captures. The distribution main may exist in the scene but reads as invisible at bay scale: no colour differentiation or flow marker distinguishes it from background structure.

Golden/tan stick figure confirmed in duct-run.png and luminaire-grid.png at floor level, at approximately [4, 0, 2] per spec. Figure reads as 1.8 m tall relative to scene elements: it occupies roughly 22 pct of the floor-to-truss span (1.8/8.0), which is geometrically correct. The figure successfully makes the 8 m clear height legible — the trunk duct at 6.8 m is clearly high above the figure's head, and the luminaires at 7.0 m similarly high.

defects.description: The compressor-skid camera preset frames only the two compressor cabinets. The receiver tank (0.91 m dia x 2.36 m tall, blue) and dryer (0.8x0.6x1.4 m) are cut off to the right of the frame. The spec explicitly promises the skid identity includes a vertical receiver and a dryer alongside the compressors; the dedicated evidence shot cannot support that promise.

The compressor-skid view faces the back/shadow side of the compressor packages relative to the house-rig key light. The resulting image is near-black; the cooling-fan grille circles that identify the machines as rotary-screw packages are barely visible. The dedicated framing for a critical feature must be lit so that the identity features are readable.

Eight diffusers (spec: diffuser_count 8, diffuser_array from x=-10 to x=14 at y=6.55, attached to trunk_duct_underside) are not distinguishable as individual outlet shapes in any of the 11 captures. The green flow arrows indicate air direction along the duct but do not substitute for the diffuser geometry. Diffusers may be absent or their blockout geometry may be too small to resolve at the capture scale.

Compressed air distribution main (0.08 m dia, 29.5 m run at 2.36-5.5 m height) is not visible in any interior or hero view. The HVAC trunk duct (0.95 m dia, 12x larger) visually dominates all interior captures. The distribution main is a key narrative element (it is how the compressed air reaches the process demand); it should be visually distinct.

corrections.description: Revise the compressor-skid camera preset to (a) pull back far enough that both compressor packages, the receiver, and the dryer are all in frame simultaneously, and (b) orbit to a position that faces a surface illuminated by the house-rig key light so the fan-grille circles and the blue receiver cylinder are both readable. The receiver at 2.36 m must read visibly taller than the 1.7 m compressor cabinets in the corrected frame.

Verify that diffuser_array geometry (8 outlet meshes from x=-10 to x=14 at y=6.55 on the trunk duct underside) is present in the scene. If absent, add the 8 diffuser meshes per the spec attachment. If present but too small, increase outlet diameter to at least 0.25 m (blockout voxel resolution) or add a visible flow-cone indicator per diffuser to make the count verifiable in the duct-run capture.

Distinguish the compressed air distribution main from the HVAC trunk duct by applying the stainless-pipe material (colour #d2d6d8, metalness 0.9) and adding at least one green flow arrow marker along its 29.5 m run. A pipe at 2.36-5.5 m height running the bay length should be visible in the hero view against the darker wall background.
